items.title: 'It becomes never-ending': Carnival cruise crew reveal punishing conditions
items.description: Passengers boarding a Carnival cruise ship are promised a world of endless food, relaxation and oceanic luxury. But for the crew who make these escapes possible, life is vastly different.

items.title: Battery-powered households not signing up to 'virtual power plant' scheme
items.description: Thousands of households with batteries installed under the federal government's scheme are choosing not to sign up to be a so-called virtual power plant that sells stored energy back to the grid.

items.title: Melbourne 'hero' shop owner dies from alleged assault injuries
items.description: Van Viet Truong, 60, was hailed as a hero after coming to the aid of a fellow retail worker after five youths tried to rob a store in Sunshine.

items.title: Labor's migration test looks different to Howard's
items.description: If stopping asylum seeker boats was the great immigration challenge in decades past, achieving a lower Net Overseas Migration (NOM) figure has become the new political test.

items.title: Live: Hanson 'doesn't care' if businesses are impacted by permanent migration cut
items.description: Pauline Hanson says she doesn't care if Labor's proposed cuts to skilled and family visas impact Australian businesses. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: ACT Opposition Leader admits to texting 'f*** my job is boring' during hearing
items.description: ACT Opposition Leader Mark Parton has admitted he sent a text message complaining about how boring his job is during budget estimates.

items.title: Three charged for 'threats' amid probe into Black US teens' shady death
items.description: Three people have been charged for allegedly threatening a US judge, authorities and witnesses connected to the investigation of black teenager Nolan Wells's mysterious death.

items.title: The Michigan result that could set the tone for the midterms in November
items.description: Abdul El-Sayed's victory over Haley Stevens in the Democrats' Michigan primary race could shape the party's messaging to voters and how it responds to Donald Trump ahead of November's crucial midterms.

items.title: Year by year, Sydney's winter wonderland is fading into memory
items.description: New South Wales is in the middle of its 30th consecutive warmer than average winter — and a past staple of the season is rapidly vanishing.

items.title: Live: ASX hits record high for second day running
items.description: The Australian share market opens at record high in morning trading. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Wall Street debt binge could end in tears — and lost billions
items.description: Credit default swaps for US big tech companies are soaring to record highs. It means investors are fearful of a major Wall Street company collapse.

items.title: Netball's uniform debacle hints at bigger problem for women in sport
items.description: Swifts netballer and professional nutritionist Teigan O'Shannassy says uniform problems are just one of the many difficulties elite female athletes struggling with body image issues face.

items.title: 'Rare and beautiful': Owl population booms following mouse plague
items.description: Clutches of barn owl chicks found inside a grain silo and cockatoo boxes indicate a "smorgasbord" of food, experts say.

items.title: 'Papa, when will you be home?' The hidden cost of the fuel discount ending
items.description: A taxi driver says he is driving 12 hours a day and considering a second job to make ends meet amid rising fuel prices.

items.title: 'Defining image' appears on 50-cent coin entering circulation
items.description: The Royal Australian Mint is encouraging people to check their change for the new 50-cent coin.

items.title: Gillian Anderson on how Nicole Kidman led her to take more risks
items.description: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma sees the X-Files star take on a beguiling role as a reclusive former final girl.

items.title: Can you tell which movies were filmed in Australia?
items.description: The Australian film industry has a long and rich history of pretending local sets are exotic places. Put your film knowledge to the test with our quiz.

items.title: We've never seen the Sun in this much detail before
items.description: The highest-resolution imagery of the Sun's surface ever taken reveals dizzying currents, and clues about our star's magnetic fields.

items.title: More alleged victims surface in child sex abuse case against paediatrician
items.description: A Perth paediatrician who allegedly recorded himself abusing children in his clinic is charged with another 15 child sex offences against seven more alleged victims.

items.title: Toddler found safe after woman and man died in suspected murder-suicide
items.description: A 23-year-old woman and 45-year-old man are found dead at a property in Charleville in outback Queensland after a toddler was taken to hospital.

items.title: Is Jetstar's new bag policy really just following the rest of the world?
items.description: Jetstar says charging passengers to use overhead lockers brings it into line with many overseas low-cost airlines. But is "unbundling" fees and charges actually making it more expensive to fly budget?

items.title: Inquest into mother's death examines Albury Hospital transfer delays
items.description: A coronial inquest into Kate Manley's death at Albury Hospital hears about communication issues between psychiatric and medical units.

items.title: First home buyers enter market in outback city where median house price is $312K
items.description: An outback city known for its rodeos and red dirt is home to one of the youngest average populations in Australia. With so many under 35s flocking to Mount Isa, it might be an opportunity to step into the housing market.

items.title: Parents warned not to 'shy away' from NAPLAN results
items.description: Parents concerned about their children's latest NAPLAN results are being encouraged to foster a love of language at home.

items.title: AI model used fake identities 'unprompted' to deceive humans in a safety test
items.description: The British government's AI Security Institute has released a report showing AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic had, in test conditions, engaged in "harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".
